articles.description: Starting September 11, manufacturers of AI agent products placed on the EU market must report actively exploited vulnerabilities within 24 hours, with penalties up to 15 million euros or 2.5% of global turnover.

articles.title: JAKA Robotics strikes back at Teradyne in European patent dispute over collaborative robot technology
articles.description: Chinese cobot maker JAKA has taken legal action against Teradyne Robotics to stop what it calls false and misleading public statements about patent infringement, escalating the dispute at the Unified Patent Court.
articles.content: JAKA's response follows Teradyne's UPC filing in Copenhagen against JAKA's German subsidiary. The case highlights intensifying competition in the European collaborative robot market, where established players are using patent litigation to challenge Chinese competitors entering the EU market.

articles.title: Council of Europe drafts privacy rules for AI chatbots and agents covering 55 nations
articles.description: The Council of Europe has published draft guidelines under Convention 108+ addressing chatbot memory, AI agent autonomy, and training-data leaks, with Bureau review scheduled for September 16-17.
articles.content: The draft extends privacy protections beyond GDPR's reach to 55 nations, addressing risks specific to AI agents including memory persistence, autonomous data processing, and training-data leakage. The guidelines represent the first multilateral attempt to regulate AI privacy across jurisdictional boundaries.

articles.title: Quantum Foundry Copenhagen announces 5,300-square-meter quantum chip fabrication facility
articles.description: Quantum Foundry Copenhagen and the Novo Nordisk Foundation have announced plans to establish a 5,300 sqm quantum chip fabrication facility in Copenhagen, opening in 2027 to strengthen Europe's quantum manufacturing capabilities.
articles.content: The facility will be tailored to the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme and aims to develop a generally applicable quantum computer. It represents a significant step in building European sovereignty in quantum hardware, addressing a gap left by the dominance of US and Chinese quantum initiatives.

articles.title: US Commerce Secretary Lutnick says semiconductor tariffs are coming: 'Build in America or pay'
articles.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick announced the Trump administration is preparing semiconductor tariffs with carveouts for companies that build chip facilities in the United States, with implications for European semiconductor supply chains.

articles.description: Following NIST's 2024 post-quantum cryptography algorithm standardisation, the UK-based PQShield has been selected to assist in mapping varied global rules for quantum-safe algorithm transitions, including the NSA's ban on hybrid approaches.
articles.content: PQShield's role involves harmonising post-quantum cryptography migration guidance across different national frameworks, addressing inconsistencies between the NSA's approach, EU policies, and other global standards. The work is critical as organisations worldwide face a deadline to transition from quantum-vulnerable encryption before quantum computers can break current cryptographic systems.

articles.content: The analysis examines Europe's semiconductor strategy following the Digital Omnibus amendments and the shift from volume targets to strategic indispensability. articles.title: Exail delivers space-grade laser for Europe's CARIOQA quantum gravimetry mission
articles.description: French photonics company Exail has delivered a space-qualified laser source to CNES for Europe's CARIOQA quantum pathfinder mission, advancing quantum sensing capabilities in space.
articles.content: The CARIOQA mission, funded by the Horizon Europe Programme, aims to demonstrate quantum sensing capabilities in orbit by operating a quantum accelerometer in space. Exail's laser source is a critical component for the quantum gravimetry Pathfinder Mission, which could enable ultra-precise Earth and climate monitoring from space.

articles.title: Apple's Siri AI launches September 9 with waitlist and complete EU block due to DMA
articles.description: Apple's rebuilt Gemini-powered Siri AI arrives on iOS 27 waitlisted and English-only, with the EU completely blocked over Digital Markets Act requirements for third-party assistant access.
articles.content: Apple confirmed the EU block stems from DMA rules requiring equal device access for rival voice assistants. Apple proposed a Trusted System Agent architecture as an alternative, but the European Commission rejected it. Approximately 450 million iPhone and iPad users in the EU are affected, with no timeline for availability. Siri AI also faces regulatory delays in China.

articles.description: Matt Clifford, the architect of the UK's AI Growth Zones plan and chair of ARIA, has joined Anthropic as Global Affairs managing director, raising conflict-of-interest concerns from UK MPs.

Clifford stated the most important AI decisions will be made by companies and governments together.

articles.description: Google introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash with improvements in coding and agentic tasks, alongside Flash Cyber for vulnerability detection and automated patching available to trusted defenders.
articles.content: Flash Cyber is Google's most capable cybersecurity model with frontier-level performance in vulnerability detection. Flash Cyber is available through Google's new Fairwind Program for trusted defenders, reflecting growing concerns about AI-powered cyber threats.

articles.description: EU antitrust regulators are seeking feedback from publishers on Google's proposal to let them opt out of AI search features without affecting their regular search rankings.

Google announced its AI opt-out in June 2026, the same day the UK antitrust watchdog ordered similar measures. articles.title: TSMC says Europe's chip strategy is shifting from factory construction to demand creation
articles.description: TSMC reports that Europe's semiconductor push is moving beyond factory building toward demand development, design support, and talent building across the continent.
articles.content: The assessment comes as TSMC's Dresden fab in Saxony progresses toward production. The shift signals maturity in Europe's chip strategy: having secured manufacturing capacity through the Chips Act, attention now turns to building the design ecosystem and skilled workforce needed for self-sustaining semiconductor innovation rather than import-dependent fabs.

articles.title: Germany's Uplift Ventures debuts EUR100 million fund to bridge Europe's DeepTech financing gap
articles.description: Uplift Ventures launched its inaugural EUR100 million venture capital fund to back European deep tech companies from Seed to Series A, targeting one of the largest financing gaps in the European tech ecosystem.
articles.content: The Hamburg- and Berlin-based venture platform aims to close the funding gap between seed and growth stages for European DeepTech startups. The fund will invest in high-growth technology companies and select deep-tech venture capital funds across Europe, focusing on areas including AI, robotics, and advanced manufacturing. The launch comes amid record European AI investment, with startups capturing 55% of all VC capital in H1 2026.

articles.title: European Commission begins AI Act enforcement against 30+ companies and discusses cyber risks with OpenAI and Anthropic
articles.description: The European Commission has sent Requests for Information to over 30 AI companies, marking the first enforcement actions under the AI Act. Brussels confirmed recent exchanges with OpenAI and Anthropic about cybersecurity risks.
articles.content: The Commission's RFIs cover two areas: safety and security of AI systems including general-purpose models, and copyright and transparency obligations. The Commission has not disclosed which companies received the requests but confirmed direct discussions with OpenAI and Anthropic about cyber risks. ENISA continues bilateral onboarding discussions with companies to establish security standards for advanced model access.

articles.description: The United States pressed G20 members to take a light-touch approach to AI regulation, while Elon Musk slammed EU tech rules as inhibiting innovation. The EU continues to push its comprehensive AI Act framework.
articles.content: At the G20 tech ministerial in Chapel Hill, the US called for deregulation emphasizing industry growth over regulatory constraints. Musk criticized the EU's regulatory approach and defended AI data centre construction. The divide highlights the growing transatlantic gap on AI governance, with the EU maintaining its first-mover regulatory framework while the US favours innovation-first policies.
